races.name: Randox Rated Hurdle

runners_data.name: Chanceawetmorning
runners_data.note: Six-year-old Gordon Elliott runner in fine nick with two recent wins at 16f on Good; Jack Williamson's 5lb claim is replaced here by Josh Williamson, and the 56-day gap is worth monitoring, but the prominent style suits this uncontested pace shape perfectly.

runners_data.name: Cosmos d'Ainay
runners_data.note: Jack Kennedy takes the ride for Gordon Elliott on this lightly-raced six-year-old who won most recently at 17f on Good and boasts a perfect 2W4P record on similar going; prominent style and strong recent form make this one of the most naturally positioned horses in the race.

runners_data.name: Malbay Madness
runners_data.note: Hold-up operator with two wins from recent starts at 16-18f on Good, but the genuine off-the-pace style means it needs a sufficient gallop from lone front-runner Trasna Na Pairce to land a blow; headgear (hood) worn and trainer T14 record of 0/5 offers little support.

runners_data.name: Trasna Na Pairce
runners_data.note: The only confirmed front-runner in this field who will control the tempo from the start; wears blinkers and a hood for De Bromhead, last ran 18 days ago, and its form string of 0-5274 on Good raises questions about winning ability even when on a comfortable lead.

runners_data.name: Cap Bernat
runners_data.note: Thirteen-year-old veteran returning from a 420-day absence for Robin McNeilly who has no runners in the past 14 days; placed on Good at 19f previously but the layoff is a significant concern, and the prominent style will keep it in contention early even if fitness fades late.

runners_data.name: Shinnhill
runners_data.note: Front-running type at heart who won at 18f on Good for Neil McKnight, but with Chanceawetmorning, Cosmos d'Ainay, and Cap Bernat all wanting prominent spots, Shinnhill is squeezed into a midfield berth it won't relish; 86-day absence and a style-fit score of 0.92 compound the concern.

runners_data.name: Tribal Moon
runners_data.note: Lightly-weighted five-year-old for amateur rider Ms E Dunseath, who runs just eight days after its last start; genuine hold-up profile but form shows limited placed efforts and a best recent finish of third at 22f, making it reliant on a faster-than-expected pace to get competitive.

races.paceDynamic: Trasna Na Pairce is the sole confirmed front-runner and should dictate from the off against a field of seven over 2m2f on Good ground at Downpatrick, setting a sustainable and uncontested gallop that keeps the tempo controlled rather than scorching. Chanceawetmorning, Cosmos d'Ainay, and Cap Bernat are the prominent types who will track close to the pace, creating a compact early order that is unlikely to string the field out. Malbay Madness and Tribal Moon sit as genuine hold-up horses and will need the pace to be sufficient to reel in the leaders in the home straight, though with only one true front-runner the pace may lack the urgency they require. The field holds more prominent types than can all occupy those early positions simultaneously — Shinnhill is a natural prominent racer but is mapped to midfield given the congestion ahead, making it unlikely to secure its preferred pitch. This race shape strongly favours prominent-to-leading-tracked horses that can travel close to Trasna Na Pairce and strike from the front end when the tempo eases, rewarding those with tactical fluency over pure staying power.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Lead, Front Tracked
scenarios.trigger: If Trasna Na Pairce bowls along at a sustainable clip and the prominent tracking horses travel sweetly into the home straight.
scenarios.body: Trasna Na Pairce sets an uncontested pace that allows the race to develop at a fair but manageable tempo, with Chanceawetmorning and Cosmos d'Ainay poised to pounce jumping the last; the Good ground and lack of pace pressure suits horses with class and jumping fluency who can quicken from a close-up position.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Pounces Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is faster than expected and the front end ties itself up in the closing stages.
scenarios.body: A stronger-than-anticipated gallop from Trasna Na Pairce burns off the prominent trackers approaching the home turn, leaving Malbay Madness to come from off the pace with a sustained run; Malbay Madness has winning form at 18f on Good and a recent win in class, making it the most credible closer in the field.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Front Runner Holds On
scenarios.trigger: If Trasna Na Pairce dictates at a very gentle pace and the prominent trackers are unable to quicken past it jumping the last.
scenarios.body: With no pressure on the leader and the race run at a crawl, Trasna Na Pairce conserves enough energy to outstay challengers in the final 150 yards; De Bromhead's runner is fresh off an 18-day break, wears a hood to aid concentration, and its two-win-from-five-run profile on Good ground supports durability at the head of affairs.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Midfield Shuffler Gets Through
scenarios.trigger: If interference or jumping errors disrupt the prominent horses and a horse from off the pace threads through late.
scenarios.body: Shinnhill, racing out of its natural prominent position in midfield due to field congestion, would need a troubled run for rivals and a clean passage to produce its best; its style-fit discount and long 86-day absence make this a low-probability outcome even if the scenario materialises.

watchPoints.text: Cosmos d'Ainay and Chanceawetmorning both represent Gordon Elliott and want prominent early positions — watch for a possible stable tactics scenario where one sets the fractions and the other delivers the winning move.
Trasna Na Pairce sets a very comfortable pace with no pressing rival — if the tempo is too slow, the horse may have enough left in the tank to hold on, compromising the prominent trackers' finish.

Cap Bernat returns from 420 days off and has not run since last year — watch for signs of rustiness jumping or a quick fade from the second-last hurdle onwards, which could create trouble for horses tracking behind.

Shinnhill's natural front-running instinct may cause it to push forward out of its mapped midfield position in the early stages — if it does, the congestion among prominent runners could lead to crowding on the first circuit.

Tribal Moon runs for the second time in eight days under a 7lb claimer — monitor its jumping fluency early, as inexperienced riders on fresh horses at Downpatrick's undulating track can struggle to find a rhythm over hurdles.

races.name: Lily O'Hare Memorial Handicap Hurdle

runners_data.name: Kalsman
runners_data.note: Has winning form at 20f on Good going (won four runs back) and a previous Downpatrick placing; genuine hold-up type who stays well and has handled this course and conditions before — 57 days off is not a concern with Liam Lennon's yard.

runners_data.name: Pralognan
runners_data.note: Brings some class from A J Martin's yard but has not run in 255 days and drops back to a shorter trip than recent assignments; a true hold-up horse whose last victory came over further — fitness question is real after such a long absence.

runners_data.name: Tropical Twist
runners_data.note: Won last time out 2 days ago at 17f on Good, so connections are clearly happy to run quickly back; Jack Kennedy is an elite jockey upgrade and Gordon Elliott's string is in form (T14: 2/42) — natural hold-up type who can travel and quicken.

runners_data.name: Augusta George
runners_data.note: The one genuine prominent runner in the field beyond Parkgarve, with a course win at 19f and placed effort at 22f at Downpatrick on Good — strong course-and-distance form makes this a meaningful player in any scenario where the pace is steady.

runners_data.name: Parkgarve
runners_data.note: Lone confirmed front-runner who should dictate from the break; however, the STYLE_FIT flag (0.90) suggests this role is slightly out of character, and a recent run just 23 days ago and a modest form string (0-8654) temper confidence despite the positional advantage.

runners_data.name: Barrogstown Girl
runners_data.note: Naturally a hold-up horse — her best effort was a second at 19f on Good — but redistributed toward midfield on the map because the field is saturated with rear-runners; STYLE_FIT (0.92) slightly discounts her chance if she cannot get a clean run from her true position.

runners_data.name: Leitzel
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with an uninspiring recent string of 3000-0 and consistently finishing mid-to-rear in similar events on Good; 97 days off and a 5lb claimer (Alan O'Sullivan) do little to inspire confidence despite a relatively clear run likely from behind.

runners_data.name: Fine Print
runners_data.note: Showed a placed effort at 14f on Standard, suggesting a shorter, faster trip suits better than today's 2m2f; a natural closer who is mapped toward midfield by necessity — the extra distance looks a concern and the STYLE_FIT tag (0.92) is relevant.

runners_data.name: Granlahan
runners_data.note: Young 4-year-old with a consistent placed record on Good going (3rd three times in last five) and the services of Darragh O'Keeffe is a positive; true hold-up type shuffled toward midfield on the map — if he can get back to his natural position, his finishing effort could be significant.

runners_data.name: Gortmore Lady
runners_data.note: Showed a third at 18f on Good recently but a subsequent pulled-up run and a sequence of question marks in the form book around distance coverage raise doubts; hold-up type mapped mid by redistribution, and the amateur rider (Mr J Costello, 7lb) adds risk.

runners_data.name: Mount Hotham
runners_data.note: Flagged as a horse that fades in the finish, which is a significant tactical liability in any scenario — this is a horse who gets into contention but cannot sustain his effort; Danny Mullins is a quality pilot but the pattern of form makes him vulnerable at the business end.

runners_data.name: La Rocca Lass
runners_data.note: Dual "fades in finish" flag and an all-zeros form string (0000-0 in last five) leaves very little to recommend; runs off the lowest weight in the field (142lbs) but a true hold-up horse displaced to midfield, and the form gives no reason to expect a turnaround.

races.paceDynamic: Parkgarve is the one confirmed front-runner in this 12-runner field and, with no genuine rival willing to press them from the outset, should control proceedings at a sustainable, even gallop on Good ground over 2m2f at Downpatrick. That uncontested lead creates a rail-hugging, controlled tempo that will not be punishing enough to crack a horse with jumping fluency and fitness, meaning prominently-placed types who can track without burning energy are best placed to pounce. The majority of this field — Barrogstown Girl, Fine Print, Granlahan, Gortmore Lady, Mount Hotham and La Rocca Lass — are true hold-up horses redistributed into mid-pack on the map because there are more closer types than the shape can accommodate at the rear; in reality, Augusta George is best-placed to shadow Parkgarve from a genuine prominent position. A single-paced, moderately-run race at Good tempo on a sharp circuit like Downpatrick historically rewards horses who travel close to the pace and jump fluently, making the prominent-to-midfield profile the decisive tactical advantage today.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Parkgarve Controls, Closers Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If Parkgarve dictates a steady, uncontested lead and the field settles into a compressed bunch, allowing tractable hold-up types to make smooth headway from two out.
scenarios.body: Parkgarve sets an honest but not demanding pace, keeping rivals tight behind them on the sharp Downpatrick circuit; genuine hold-up horses with finishing pace — Kalsman, Tropical Twist — have enough room to pick their way through and hit the line strongly.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Scores
scenarios.trigger: If Augusta George or a similarly-placed tracker maintains a perfect pitch just behind Parkgarve, takes over turning in, and the pace is too slow for late closers to generate momentum.
scenarios.body: A gentle gallop suits the horse who can conserve energy close to the pace and pounce early at the second-last, leaving true hold-up runners too much to do on the short run-in.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Strong Closer Delivers Late
scenarios.trigger: If Granlahan or Pralognan — each with legitimate hold-up form — manages to secure a genuine rearward position and the pace quickens sufficiently to create a true stamina test in the final half-mile.
scenarios.body: Granlahan's consistent placed form on Good ground and Pralognan's earlier class give both the profile to benefit if the tempo honestly tests rivals; the key caveat is that several mapped midfielders are not genuine hold-up types, reducing the chance of a clean late run.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Race Breaks Down, Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses or there are jumping errors mid-race that fracture the field and create a sprint finish from an unusual position.
scenarios.body: A disorderly race without a clean flow through the middle stages randomises the outcome; Tropical Twist, with recent winning form and a sharp jockey in Jack Kennedy, is well-equipped to adapt mid-race.

watchPoints.text: Tropical Twist is 2 days off a win with Jack Kennedy booked — watch for early confirmation she has travelled well overnight; if she settles sweetly in the first mile she could be the one who most threatens to close from off the pace.

Augusta George is the only horse with both genuine prominent form and strong Downpatrick course-and-distance credentials — watch her position rounding the first bend; if she slots into second behind Parkgarve she controls the race shape entirely.

Parkgarve's STYLE_FIT flag (0.90) means the front-running role is not fully natural — watch the opening two furlongs for any sign she is being held up rather than asked to stride on, which would collapse the dominant pace scenario instantly.

Granlahan is a 4-year-old with Darragh O'Keeffe and a tidy placed record, but is likely to be forced wide or further back than ideal given the volume of hold-up horses — watch where he ends up after the first hurdle to gauge whether he can produce a meaningful late challenge.

Mount Hotham and La Rocca Lass both carry the "fades in finish" flag — if either is prominent turning for home they may cause interference or a positional squeeze on genuine closers as they back up; riders behind them should be alert in the final half-mile.

races.name: Franco Hughes Away Bet Mares Handicap Hurdle

runners_data.name: Cobra Queen
runners_data.note: Outstanding record on Good ground (14/15, four wins) and Henry De Bromhead in solid recent form; genuine hold-up horse who needs a true-run race to deliver her turn of foot, and the 2m6f trip suits her stamina profile.

runners_data.name: Samba Train
runners_data.note: The sole front-runner in this 12-runner field, Mark Walsh's ride for Bolger, winning last time out; has run eight times on Good with three wins and four places — pace-setter who will set the shape and must be respected throughout.

runners_data.name: Billie Frechette
runners_data.note: A hold-up horse with trainer Noel Meade 2/25 over 14 days and last in the 16-runner field last time; the amateur rider and step up from shorter trips are factors, and she will need others to cut out the work.

runners_data.name: Theflyingbee
runners_data.note: Prominent racer with a consistent recent profile of placed efforts on Good ground, though 87 days off the track and a 9-year-old on the upgrade is a risk; amateur rider Martin (7) adds uncertainty in a congested prominent group.

runners_data.name: Camlin Park
runners_data.note: Prominent style but a patchy record (only 3/5 on Good ground, 1 win from 5 similar) and ran poorly at 7/16f last time; headgear noted, and a genuinely small sample of relevant form makes this difficult to trust in a competitive field.

runners_data.name: Poetic Twist
runners_data.note: Jack Kennedy's mount for Gordon Elliott, a horse with a remarkable record of four places in five starts — a consistent performer on Good ground who has the class and jockey profile to exploit the prominent congestion from just off the pace.

runners_data.name: Gangster Granny
runners_data.note: Sean Flanagan rides a horse with three wins from 10 Good-ground runs and two recent wins at 2m2f; the step up to 2m6f is an open question, though the Good going suits and she will track from midfield.

runners_data.name: Joya Del Mar
runners_data.note: A genuine hold-up type with two wins on Good ground, though the 8-year-old's last five runs include a 13th and variability; Patrick O'Brien (5) on board and the class concern around OR=106 over 2m6f is real.

runners_data.name: Oh Janey
runners_data.note: Prominent racer with one win from nine relevant starts and modest recent form (5th, 6th); headgear worn, Sam Ewing rides, and the form string of 416-65 does not inspire confidence in a competitive mares' heat.

runners_data.name: Shannon Bank
runners_data.note: Lightly-traded trainer Kinirons, 40 days off, recent form of 2P-717 is unremarkable; this is a true hold-up horse whose chance is tempered by being mapped into midfield — operating ahead of her natural position in a pace-light race reduces her effectiveness.

runners_data.name: Miss Lia
runners_data.note: P J Rothwell's runner has strong placing form on soft/heavy ground (two 2nds) but her recent Good-ground record is weaker; the 57-day absence and OR=93 make her vulnerable, and being a natural hold-up type unable to slot to the rear further limits her opportunity here.

runners_data.name: Steps In The Sand
runners_data.note: Amateur rider Costello (7), just three days since last run — a very quick turnaround which is unusual and worth monitoring; prominent style on a light weight of 140lbs, though the form string 88-434 signals consistency without the class to win.

races.paceDynamic: Samba Train is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with only one horse willing to lead, will dictate from the front at a sustainable, controlled gallop on Good ground over 2m6f — this is a race likely to be won from the front or just off it. Five horses — Theflyingbee, Camlin Park, Poetic Twist, Oh Janey, and Steps In The Sand — all want prominent positions, creating significant congestion and traffic risk from the second-last hurdle, as they bunch on a single pace-setter's heels. Shannon Bank and Miss Lia are genuine hold-up types who cannot realistically get to the rear of a field this small and pace-light, having been mapped to midfield because the rear is already occupied by Cobra Queen, Gangster Granny, and Joya Del Mar — those are the true closers, and Shannon Bank and Miss Lia are unlikely to be able to operate from their natural position. The tactical verdict is clear: this race shape most favours prominent racers who can settle just off Samba Train and pick up early in the straight, and hold-up horses that can travel smoothly in midfield when their preferred back-of-the-field slot is unavailable.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Samba Train Controls Throughout
scenarios.trigger: If Samba Train is allowed to dictate an honest but uncontested gallop and the prominent pack fails to mount a coordinated challenge.
scenarios.body: Samba Train sets a measured pace from the front and, with no rival willing to seriously pressurise, quickens clear from the last hurdle with stamina conserved; Mark Walsh's positional intelligence at Downpatrick will be a key asset over this 2m6f trip.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Posse Overwhelms Leader
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent cluster of Theflyingbee, Poetic Twist, and Camlin Park press Samba Train from early and the pace lifts enough to stop the leader from conserving energy.
scenarios.body: The heightened tempo burns off Samba Train approaching the home turn, leaving the strongest traveller in the prominent group — ideally one ridden by a claiming jockey who can exploit a gap — to sweep through; Poetic Twist's record of four placings in five recent starts on Good ground marks her out as the prime beneficiary.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Pounce Late
scenarios.trigger: If the race develops into a true test of stamina at a genuine clip and the closers get an unimpeded run from two out.
scenarios.body: Cobra Queen's outstanding record on Good ground (14/15 with four wins) gives her the class to close from off the pace, and Gangster Granny's recent wins at 2m2f on Good ground suggest she stays well enough to finish powerfully; however, with Samba Train likely to set only a sustainable pace, the late closers may find the tempo has not been searching enough to reel in the leader.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos And Traffic Derails Fancied Runners
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent congestion causes interference, jumping errors, or forced checking between the third-last and second-last hurdle that disrupts multiple market principles.
scenarios.body: With five horses competing for the same three or four prominent slots, a faltering jumper or a rider forced wide could derail Poetic Twist or Camlin Park and hand the advantage to a horse that has tracked without issue; Steps In The Sand or Oh Janey, carrying light weights and untroubled by the melee, could creep into contention at a big price.

watchPoints.text: Samba Train (front-runner) — watch whether any prominent horse challenges for the lead before halfway; if the pace is genuinely uncontested Mark Walsh can dictate terms that are very hard to overcome.

Prominent congestion danger 2-3 out — Theflyingbee, Camlin Park, Poetic Twist, Oh Janey, and Steps In The Sand all want the same ground; a jumping error or checked stride from any of these could cause interference at a critical point.

Cobra Queen — watch her position at halfway; if the pace is too slow she risks getting caught in the midfield traffic rather than swooping from a clear last position, which is where her Good-ground form is built.

Steps In The Sand — three days since last run is an unusually short turnaround; watch the betting market for any signs of market support or drift that might indicate whether connections are confident.

Shannon Bank and Miss Lia — both true hold-up horses who are unable to get to their natural position in this field; monitor whether either can find a clear passage from midfield in the straight, as their finishing efforts may be compromised by racing out of role.

races.name: J Murdoch Contracts Maiden Hurdle

runners_data.name: G N Jefferson
runners_data.note: Prominent-racing five-year-old for John McConnell with a fading-finish flag to note; three runs on Good ground without a win or place suggests a recurring pattern of stopping late, and at 2m6f that tendency is a real concern.

runners_data.name: I Can Find Em
runners_data.note: Gary McGill's five-year-old has shown a placing at 2m2f on Good but is a true hold-up horse whose position will be compromised in a field already stacked with closers, diluting its chance in a race not likely to be run at a searching enough gallop.

runners_data.name: Lygon Lad
runners_data.note: Jack Kennedy takes the ride for Gordon Elliott on a horse absent for 490 days, and while that layoff is the dominant concern, its natural closer style will also be squeezed — it needs the field to be strung out to deliver, which an uncontested lead scenario does not provide.

runners_data.name: Paymelater
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer with ten qualifying Good-ground runs behind it and two places from twelve; the trip is within range but an uncontested pace set by That's It Paddy is unlikely to produce the strong gallop this horse needs to produce its best from the rear.

runners_data.name: That's It Paddy
runners_data.note: The lone front-runner who will have things entirely its own way from the flag; last run was 89 days ago and form reads 4P-6, so durability at 2m6f is an open question, but its ability to dictate the pace map is the central tactical fact of this race.

runners_data.name: Young Doran
runners_data.note: Showed a solid second on debut over 2m2f on Good, which is the most encouraging recent form line in this field; with only one run to his name he is lightly raced but that staying profile at a mile and three furlongs bodes well for stepping up to 2m6f.

runners_data.name: Magical Sal
runners_data.note: J J Slevin partners this six-year-old who has form figures of 2 and 3 on Good ground and is wearing a hood; a genuine hold-up type by nature, it will be working against its own instincts if pushed into midfield, and its best chance depends on a scenario that does not suit the projected race shape.

runners_data.name: Thesilverbridle
runners_data.note: Lightly raced five-year-old for McConnell with a second on Good ground over 2m at a previous run; the unknown-style flag means positioning is genuinely unpredictable, but that recent placing is the most relevant form to the conditions here.

runners_data.name: Oops A Daisy
runners_data.note: A four-year-old with a consistent record of finishing seventh or lower across three Good-ground runs, with a fading-finish flag to reinforce the pattern; the youngest in the field and carrying the lowest weight, but the form book offers little encouragement.

races.paceDynamic: That's It Paddy is the sole confirmed front-runner in this nine-runner maiden hurdle over 2m6f at Downpatrick on Good ground, and with no rival likely to seriously contest the lead, they will set a sustainable, uncontested gallop from the outset. The pace will be honest but not punishing — a lone leader over this trip on Good ground typically sets a rhythm that compresses the field and removes any significant stamina test. Magical Sal, I Can Find Em, and Lygon Lad are all genuine hold-up types whose natural position is at the rear, but with several such horses in the field, they cannot all settle there and will be mapped into midfield, meaning the back of the race is less crowded with true closers than it appears. The tactical verdict is clear: this race shape favours prominent racers who can track That's It Paddy at close range and pounce from the second-last, as the controlled tempo will blunt the effectiveness of horses who need a truly run race to deliver a sustained late challenge.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Prompt Leader Controls
scenarios.trigger: If That's It Paddy bowls along unchallenged and sets a steady, sustainable tempo that suits a close-tracking prominent runner.
scenarios.body: That's It Paddy dictates from the front without pressure, ensuring a moderate gallop over 2m6f that keeps the race well within themselves until the home turn; prominent types who have settled in second or third position can quicken past a tiring leader from the second-last hurdle.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Battle Home
scenarios.trigger: If a second horse pushes up to challenge That's It Paddy early, lifting the tempo and turning it into a proper test of stamina.
scenarios.body: A contested pace over this trip on Good ground stretches the field and suits horses with proven stamina profiles; those who have settled just off the battle can swoop when the duelling leaders tire from the second-last.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Late Closers Swoop
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely strong enough from the front to soften the leaders and allow the hold-up horses to deliver a meaningful late challenge.
scenarios.body: Horses tracking from midfield with genuine staying power get into the race at the final hurdle as the early leaders empty; this scenario is tempered by the fact that Magical Sal, I Can Find Em, and Lygon Lad are redistributed hold-up types unlikely to have secured their natural position.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Rank Outsider Lottery
scenarios.trigger: If the field is strung out by jumping errors or unseating incidents, creating a race of attrition from an early stage.
scenarios.body: Remaining horses who jump fluently and stay on steadily inherit positions regardless of style, with the outcome driven by luck rather than tactical execution; maiden hurdle fields at this level are particularly vulnerable to this kind of chaotic race shape.

watchPoints.text: That's It Paddy's ability to last home over 2m6f is the single biggest risk in the race — if it ties up turning in, the entire pace map collapses and a prominent tracker will inherit the lead at a crucial moment.

G N Jefferson has faded in the finish across multiple Good-ground runs; if the race is run at a truly moderate tempo and he is forced to kick from the front, that tendency to stop could be exaggerated at this longer trip.

Lygon Lad's 490-day layoff under Jack Kennedy makes it a runner to monitor in the market — any unexpected support would suggest connections are confident despite the absence, but the redistribution of its hold-up role adds further uncertainty.

Magical Sal (hood, J J Slevin) has the best recent form in the field with a second over 2m2f on Good, but watch whether Slevin opts to push forward early to avoid being trapped in the hold-up crowd — if he does, the race shape changes materially.

Young Doran is the only runner in this field with a single run whose form (second over 2m2f on Good) is both recent and directly relevant to the conditions; watch for it to be ridden more prominently than its hold-up tag suggests given the compressed field.

races.name: Join Us For Ladies Day Handicap Hurdle

runners_data.name: Ocean Of Dreams
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up performer with Good-ground form (best run 9/15 sim-going starts), though only 2 places in that sample; the 5-year-old amateur rider (Mr O McGill, 5lb claim) is a notable booking factor, and 11 days since last run suggests freshness; must navigate a congested midfield to deliver a late challenge.

runners_data.name: Georgia Celena
runners_data.note: Sole confirmed front-runner here; eight-year-old mare with excellent Good-ground record (1W6P in 14 similar runs) and John McConnell a competent handler, though T14 reads 0/25 suggesting a flat patch; her style-fit tag (0.93) simply reflects that she will be racing in an uncontested lead rather than her natural prominent role — treat that as an advantage here, not a concern.

runners_data.name: Speakasyoufind
runners_data.note: Noted finisher who fades in the closing stages — a significant red flag at 2m6f; despite two placings on Good over shorter trips, the fade warning and the distance step up make her a hold-up type who may not see out the trip; P J Rothwell has had one winner from 19 in the 14-day window.

runners_data.name: My Good Pal
runners_data.note: Front-foot type with the best similar-going record among the prominent runners (1W4P in 15 runs); Gavin Cromwell a capable trainer, headgear (tongue-tie/cheekpieces) confirms this horse needs to be on the bridle early; seven-year-old who should press Georgia Celena and is the chief danger if the leader is pegged back.

runners_data.name: Sneddy Eddie
runners_data.note: Jack Kennedy is a top-class booking that elevates this 85-rated gelding considerably; a hold-up horse by nature whose form figures show modest recent finishes (0-0554), but the headgear (cheekpieces) and Kennedy's positional nous could see him delivered with a better-timed challenge than the bare form suggests.

runners_data.name: Hay Baby
runners_data.note: True hold-up horse by inclination whose actual race positioning will likely be closer to midfield given how many deep-set types populate this field; recent form figures (456-00) are uninspiring and the style-fit discount (0.91) is legitimate — Emmet Mullins sends this one out 30 days fresh but improvement is needed to factor.

runners_data.name: Ballinagaine Girl
runners_data.note: Danny Mullins takes the ride on this John Joseph Hanlon-trained mare who carries a fade-in-finish warning as well as a redistribution note — her natural rear-of-field style will be compromised by the crowded hold-up group; recent second on Soft at 20f shows ability in different conditions, but the fade flag and Good-ground questions (5 runs, no wins) are concerns.

runners_data.name: Bob The Builder
runners_data.note: Nine-year-old who has been around the track, but recent form (57-550) and a fade-in-finish warning are hard to ignore; P J Rothwell's second runner here, forced closer to midfield than his true inclination by the redistribution; limited upside at this stage of his career.

runners_data.name: Something Simple
runners_data.note: John Joseph Hanlon's third runner in the race; a hold-up horse whose recent form includes multiple pull-ups (PP-04P) — the two pulled-up runs are a serious caution; headgear (cheekpieces) suggests the stable is trying to sharpen him up, but the form profile makes him a significant risk at this trip.

runners_data.name: Sonna Lady
runners_data.note: Lightly raced four-year-old who has only raced three times, all on Good ground, finishing 10th, 7th and 9th — consistent but modest; another Hanlon inmate pushed towards midfield from her natural hold-up position; the age and inexperience over 2m6f are the key concerns in this competitive handicap.

runners_data.name: Sineads Fancy
runners_data.note: Veteran nine-year-old prominent racer with a reasonable Good-ground record (1W3P in 13 similar runs); Daniel King's claim should be respected, though T14 shows just 0/1 for trainer S Ryan; the best of the prominent types behind Georgia Celena in terms of pace profile, and a clean run from the front could see her run into the frame.

races.paceDynamic: Georgia Celena is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 11-runner field and, with no genuine rival likely to challenge her for the lead on current evidence, she should be able to dictate terms at a comfortable, sustainable clip over 2m6f on Good ground at Downpatrick. My Good Pal and Sineads Fancy are the natural prominent types who will look to sit close to her, giving the race a controlled early shape without significant pressure on the leader. The field is heavily loaded with hold-up horses — Ocean Of Dreams, Sneddy Eddie and Speakasyoufind among the genuine rearward types — meaning the race will likely develop as a slowly-run single file before quickening significantly in the final half-mile; that dynamic favours patient hold-up performers who can produce a sustained late run rather than those who need to pressurise from the front. Hay Baby, Ballinagaine Girl, Bob The Builder, Something Simple and Sonna Lady are all genuine hold-up horses in nature but have been redistributed to midfield on the map because there are far more back-of-the-field types than the race shape can physically accommodate at the rear; of these, Hay Baby and Ballinagaine Girl are most likely to actually secure a prominent-to-midfield pitch given their recent race positioning. The overall race shape — uncontested leader, moderate tempo, big field with congested midfield — most favours hold-up horses with genuine late acceleration who can thread through a tiring pack in the straight.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Georgia Celena Controls
scenarios.trigger: If Georgia Celena leads uncontested at a honest but manageable gallop and the field fails to produce a unified late challenge.
scenarios.body: Georgia Celena dictates the fractions from the front, the large hold-up contingent gets stuck in traffic or runs out of stamina when the pace quickens, and her Good-ground form (1W6P in 15 sim-going runs) proves decisive.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Late Closers Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely steady early and genuine hold-up horses find clear daylight in the straight to reel in a tiring leader.
scenarios.body: Ocean Of Dreams or Sneddy Eddie, sitting patiently in rear, benefit from a strong late run as the leader's stamina is tested at 2m6f; the key is a clear passage appearing in the final two flights.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Grind Down
scenarios.trigger: If My Good Pal or Sineads Fancy push the pace up on Georgia Celena from the outset, turning it into a true test of stamina.
scenarios.body: A stronger gallop filters out the least-effective stayers and rewards those prominent runners who can sustain their effort over the full 2m6f trip on Good ground.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Midfield Chaos Intervenes
scenarios.trigger: If the congested midfield group produces a late melee, with traffic issues and interference redistributing the finish order unpredictably.
scenarios.body: Ballinagaine Girl or Hay Baby, forced out of their natural hold-up role and racing closer than ideal, benefit if they find a clear run earlier than expected and the front-runners capitulate; their style-fit discounts and fade warnings make this a low-probability route to the frame.

watchPoints.text: Georgia Celena must be watched in the early stages — if she is allowed a completely uncontested lead by My Good Pal and Sineads Fancy, her Good-ground front-running form could prove very difficult to peg back in an 11-runner field that will be bunched behind her.

My Good Pal is the key pace challenger to watch; if Gavin Cromwell's runner is sent forward aggressively by Mr B M Coonan to press Georgia Celena, it could materially increase the tempo and open the race up for hold-up horses like Ocean Of Dreams or Sneddy Eddie.

Congestion in the midfield and rear is a serious risk at Downpatrick over 2m6f with 11 runners — horses like Hay Baby, Ballinagaine Girl and Bob The Builder are all operating closer to the pace than they would naturally prefer, and a traffic incident at a hurdle flight in the back straight is a genuine danger.

Jack Kennedy on Sneddy Eddie is a significant market mover to track; if this combination drifts from a midfield position to closer than expected in the early stages, it may signal Kennedy intends a more prominent ride than the horse's recent style suggests.

Something Simple's history of pull-ups (two in recent form) means connections and the stewards may be alert to the horse's jumping — any jumping errors in the early stages from the Hanlon runners (three in total) could have a domino effect on the midfield group.
